partnership_characteristics.definition: Unincorporated business owned by two or more persons
key_features: Mutual agency (each partner can bind partnership)
partnership_characteristics.capital_accounts: Each partner has separate capital account tracking their equity

formation.contribution_of_assets: Assets contributed recorded at FAIR VALUE (not book value from partner's books)
formation.contribution_of_liabilities: If partner contributes asset with attached liability, partnership assumes liability
formation.entry_example: Partner contributes land (FV $100K) with mortgage ($40K). DR Land $100K, CR Mortgage Payable $40K, CR Partner Capital $60K
formation.goodwill_at_formation: Generally NOT recognized unless specifically agreed (use fair values of identifiable assets)

priority_order: 1. Salary allowances (if specified in partnership agreement)
income_allocation.important_note: Salaries and interest are ALLOCATIONS of income, not expenses (partnership doesn't pay salary expense to partners)
income_allocation.if_income_insufficient: Allocate in order above even if creates negative remainder (then allocate shortage per profit/loss ratio)

calculation_example_income_allocation.facts: Partnership agreement: Partner A gets $30K salary, Partner B gets $20K salary. 10% interest on beginning capital (A: $100K, B: $150K). Remainder split 60/40 (A/B). Partnership income: $100K.

calculation_example_loss_allocation.facts: Same agreement as above, but partnership loss: $(20K).
calculation_example_loss_allocation.note: Even though salaries and interest allocated, net effect is loss allocation because remainder is large negative

purchase_of_interest.description: New partner buys interest from existing partner(s) - personal transaction
purchase_of_interest.accounting: Transfer from selling partner's capital to new partner's capital. No change to total partnership capital.
purchase_of_interest.entry: DR Selling Partner Capital, CR New Partner Capital (at agreed amount)
purchase_of_interest.payment: Payment goes to selling partner personally (not to partnership)

investment_in_partnership.description: New partner invests directly in partnership - increases partnership assets and capital

three_scenarios.investment_equals_book_value: DR Cash, CR New Partner Capital (at amount invested)
three_scenarios.bonus_to_old_partners: New partner invests MORE than proportionate book value. Excess is bonus to old partners (allocated per profit ratio).
three_scenarios.bonus_to_new_partner: New partner invests LESS than proportionate book value (goodwill or special contribution). Old partners give bonus to new partner.

bonus_to_old_partners.facts: Partnership capital before admission: A $60K, B $40K (total $100K). New partner C invests $60K for 1/3 interest.

calculation.bonus_to_old_partners: $60K - $53.33K = $6.67K (split per A and B's profit ratio)

bonus_to_old_partners.entry_if_ab_split_equally: DR Cash $60K, CR A Capital $3.33K, CR B Capital $3.33K, CR C Capital $53.34K

bonus_to_new_partner.facts: Partnership capital: A $60K, B $40K (total $100K). New partner C invests $20K for 1/4 interest.

calculation.bonus_from_old_partners: $30K - $20K = $10K (taken from A and B per their ratio)

bonus_to_new_partner.entry_if_ab_split_equally: DR Cash $20K, DR A Capital $5K, DR B Capital $5K, CR C Capital $30K

withdrawal_of_partner.payment_equals_capital: DR Partner Capital, CR Cash (no bonus)
withdrawal_of_partner.payment_exceeds_capital: Bonus to withdrawing partner from remaining partners. DR Partner Capital, DR Remaining Partners' Capital (per ratio), CR Cash
withdrawal_of_partner.payment_less_than_capital: Bonus to remaining partners. DR Partner Capital, CR Remaining Partners' Capital (per ratio), CR Cash

process_steps: 1. Sell noncash assets (record gain or loss)
2. Allocate gain or loss to partners per profit/loss ratio
4. Distribute remaining cash to partners per capital balances
partnership_liquidation.right_of_offset: If partner has debit capital balance (deficit), partner must contribute to partnership. If partner cannot pay, deficit absorbed by other partners per their profit/loss ratio.
partnership_liquidation.safe_payment_schedule: Determine how much can safely be distributed to partners assuming worst case (remaining assets worthless)

liquidation_example.facts: Partnership liquidation. Capital balances: A $40K, B $30K, C $10K. Profit ratio 50/30/20. Sell all assets (BV $100K) for $70K. Pay creditors $20K.
liquidation_example.step_1_record_loss: Loss on sale: $30K. Allocate: A $(15K), B $(9K), C $(6K)

deficit_capital_balance.scenario: Partner has debit (deficit) capital balance after loss allocation
deficit_capital_balance.if_partner_pays: Partner contributes cash to eliminate deficit
deficit_capital_balance.if_partner_cannot_pay: Deficit absorbed by remaining partners per their profit/loss ratio (reducing their distributions)
deficit_capital_balance.example: C has $(5K) deficit but cannot pay. A and B absorb per their ratio (50:30 or 5:3). A absorbs $3.125K, B absorbs $1.875K.

cpa_exam_tips: Formation: Contribute assets at FAIR VALUE (not book value)
Income allocation priority: Salaries → Interest → Bonus → Remainder per ratio
Purchase of interest: No change to total partnership capital (just transfer between partners)
Investment in partnership: Increases total capital. Calculate bonus if investment ≠ proportionate BV.
Liquidation: Sell assets → Allocate gain/loss → Pay creditors → Distribute to partners per capital
Deficit capital: Partner must pay in, or remaining partners absorb per ratio

income_allocation_approach: 2. Allocate interest on capital (even if loss)
cpa_exam_strategies.admission_decision: Purchase of interest = Transfer capital. Investment = Increase capital. Check if new partner's capital = investment (no bonus) or ≠ investment (bonus exists).
cpa_exam_strategies.bonus_calculation: Total capital after admission × New partner's % = New partner's capital. Compare to investment to find bonus.
liquidation_steps: 1. Record sale of assets and gain/loss
2. Allocate gain/loss to partners per ratio
5. Distribute remaining cash per capital balances
6. If deficit: Partner pays in or other partners absorb
common_mistakes: Using book value instead of fair value at formation
Forgetting to calculate bonus when admission investment ≠ proportionate share
Not allocating deficit capital balance to remaining partners if partner can't pay

key_points: Formation: Assets at fair value, liabilities assumed
Income allocation: Salaries → Interest → Remainder per profit/loss ratio
Purchase of interest: No change to total capital (transfer between partners)
Investment in partnership: Increases capital, may create bonus
Bonus: Investment ≠ proportionate capital → Bonus to/from partners
Liquidation: Sell assets → Allocate gain/loss → Pay creditors → Distribute per capital
Deficit capital: Partner pays in or remaining partners absorb per ratio
